description: Compact default Compare rules distilled from actual small, asymmetric, selected-Memory, and large task frames. Cases are production-visible calibration, not held-out evaluation data.

rules.title: Lead with the dominant relation
rules.invariant: Explain the one relation that best characterizes both complete PRIMARY frames, such as equivalence, rule-to-instances, conditional alternatives, temporary override to baseline, general policy to specialization, shared core with a decisive difference, or no material relation.

rules.title: Spend the second sentence on the decisive difference
rules.invariant: After the dominant relation, preserve only the difference, condition, exception, or consequence most likely to change interpretation or action; do not inventory every common or side-only point.

rules.title: Keep discriminating numbers with their conditions
rules.invariant: Preserve an exact number, range, time, or date when it distinguishes the frames, and state the condition that makes the numeric difference meaningful rather than presenting two bare values.

rules.title: Describe asymmetry by semantic role
rules.invariant: When frame sizes differ, explain rule versus instances, temporary override versus baseline, or general policy versus specialization instead of reporting source counts or treating the larger frame as more authoritative.

rules.title: Keep Context evidence subordinate
rules.invariant: PRIMARY rows are the only comparison subjects. CONTEXT rows may disambiguate a PRIMARY row but must not introduce a second comparison topic, and the evidence set must cite PRIMARY material from both sides.

rules.title: Return one bounded natural paragraph
rules.invariant: Use one or two complete sentences in one paragraph, aim for roughly 45 words, and never exceed 80 whitespace-delimited words. Read the complete frozen frames, but keep output length independent of source count.

rules.title: Keep source aliases out of prose
rules.invariant: Put opaque evidence aliases only in the structured source_ids field. Never print a bare or bracketed provider alias, UID, source count, or internal evidence notation in the narrative.

rules.title: Compare peers without a hidden winner
rules.invariant: Treat REFERENCE and COMPARED as equal-authority peers unless their content itself establishes baseline, override, general, specialized, rule, or instance roles; do not call one correct merely because of its side.

rules.title: Do not impersonate the relation ledger
rules.invariant: Do not claim exhaustive disposition, assign every Memory, create Issues, recommend Meld actions, or turn the compact paragraph into a category-by-category report.

rules.title: Keep the shared primary language
rules.invariant: Write in the language shared by the PRIMARY rows. If the PRIMARY sides use different languages, use the REFERENCE primary language without translating or rewriting quoted source text.

cases.description: Two selected opening rules differ by an exact sentence bound, while unrelated neighboring structure rules remain context only.

memories.content: Complete the problem framing within the first two sentences.
Use short descriptive subheadings.
Allow a third sentence when the person, setting, or consequence would otherwise remain abstract.
Use paragraph transitions instead of extra headings.

expected.text: Both rules establish the proposal's central issue immediately. The reference caps framing at two sentences, while the compared rule permits a third only when the person, setting, or consequence would otherwise remain abstract.

known_wrong.text: The reference also favors headings while the compared frame favors paragraph transitions.
known_wrong.reason: It replaces the selected-Memory comparison with a second topic drawn only from neighboring Context evidence.

cases.description: One frame states a syntax and the other supplies conforming instances.

memories.content: Write each proposition as a lowercase letter, the exact separator is, and one lowercase word, with no terminal punctuation.
a is apple
b is banana
c is carrot

expected.text: The reference defines the lowercase letter–is–word syntax, and every compared proposition conforms to it. Their difference is semantic role rather than format: one is the governing rule and the other is its concrete instance set.

known_wrong.text: The rule matches a is apple [B1], b is banana [B2], and c is carrot [B3].
known_wrong.reason: It inventories instances and exposes provider-only evidence aliases.

cases.description: A small construction frame temporarily overrides a larger ordinary-access baseline.

memories.content: During construction, the third-floor rear entrance is closed to general passage.
During construction, the main entrance closes at 5 p.m. rather than 10 p.m.
Use the temporary step-free route beside the main entrance.
The third-floor rear entrance is normally available during opening hours.
The main entrance normally closes at 10 p.m.
The ordinary accessible route is beside the main entrance.

expected.text: The reference temporarily overrides the compared frame's normal access rules during construction. It closes the normally usable rear entrance, moves main-entry closing from 10 p.m. to 5 p.m., and substitutes a temporary step-free route for the ordinary accessible path.

known_wrong.text: The reference has three Memories and the compared frame also has three Memories about entrances.
known_wrong.reason: Counts and topic labels hide the temporary override relationship.

cases.description: A broad disclosure policy and healthcare transmission guidance share a core but differ in breadth and one retention boundary.

memories.content: Share only information necessary for the reviewed purpose and recipient.
A recipient may ordinarily retain or process a copy unless a restriction says otherwise.
Send only reviewed healthcare information after the user approves the recipient, purpose, and channel.
Silence alone establishes no permission for retention or internal processing.

expected.text: Both frames require purpose-limited disclosure and user review before transmission; the compared frame specializes that policy for healthcare. Their decisive tension is retention: the reference permits ordinary inference absent a restriction, while the healthcare guidance treats silence as no permission.

known_wrong.text: The larger reference policy is authoritative and the healthcare guidance should follow it.
known_wrong.reason: Frame size and REFERENCE position do not establish authority.

cases.description: Two single-Memory tasks share selection work but push it toward integration versus minimization.

memories.content: Combine two equal-authority advisors' policies without favoring either source.
Select which personal memories to exclude before transfer to a government healthcare agent.

expected.text: Both tasks select stored information for a new purpose, but their governance directions differ. The reference maximizes fair integration across equal-authority sources, while the compared task minimizes disclosure of sensitive personal history before transfer.

known_wrong.text: Both tasks are about Memory and therefore have essentially the same goal.
known_wrong.reason: A generic topic overlap erases the opposing integration and minimization goals.
